## Objective

Implement root Director activation, stable Task meaning, proportional workflow classification, and durable state boundaries in the two required reusable sources.

## Scope

- SKILLS-depo/task/
- ROLES-depo/project-director-ROLE.md
- Direct, decomposed, and adversarial path selection
- Audit and stopping contracts

## Entry conditions

- PHASE-001 is complete.
- The authorized write set names the two required reusable targets and excludes all protected active copies.

## Exit criteria

- The reusable Task skill loads the consumer root Director before Task work.
- The reusable Director role defines all proportional paths, ownership, state boundaries, and stopping behavior.
- Focused core-contract checks pass.

## Risks

- The two source contracts could become inconsistent.
- Wording changes could unintentionally broaden Task activation or project authority.

## TASK-003 - Make Task activation load the project Director

Revise the reusable Task skill so explicit activation resolves the exact consumer project root, reads that root ROLE.md, establishes the existing root agent as Project Director before Task work, defines Task consistently, and never creates a replacement Director or broadens authority.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Status | `completed` |
| State reason | None |
| Skip authority | None |
| Requirements | REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-018, REQ-020, REQ-022 |
| Design basis | None |
| Target artifacts | SKILLS-depo/task/SKILL.md, SKILLS-depo/task/agents/openai.yaml |
| Dependencies | TASK-002 |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | 2026-09-02T21:30:24.486068Z |

### Risks

- Ambiguous-root handling could be weakened.
- Metadata could accidentally permit implicit invocation.
- Wording could imply that loading ROLE.md spawns a Director.

### Acceptance criteria

- The reusable Task skill requires resolving AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, and ROLE.md at one exact root and reading the root ROLE.md before Task mutation, classification, or delegation.
- The contract defines a project Task as the user-given job or problem assigned to the existing root Project Director and distinguishes all named state systems.
- The skill prohibits a replacement Director, preserves explicit-only activation, and grants no new external or destructive authority.
- Metadata changes occur only if the impact matrix identifies an exact description mismatch.

### Planned verification

- Run the Task package structural validator.
- Inspect the normalized contract for exact root-role activation, no-replacement, explicit-only, and authority-boundary clauses.
- Run focused negative checks for ambiguous roots and wording that implies spawning a second Director.

## TASK-004 - Define proportional Director execution paths

Revise the reusable Project Director role to assess complexity and uncertainty, choose direct work for simple tasks, decompose separable complex work, or choose adversarial candidate solutions for nondecomposable uncertainty, while honoring feasible explicit user orchestration.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Status | `completed` |
| State reason | None |

| Requirements | REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-019, REQ-020, REQ-022 |

| Dependencies | TASK-003 |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | 2026-09-02T21:31:37.917474Z |

### Risks

- A fixed scoring rule could replace evidence-based judgment.
- Delegation language could become mandatory for trivial work or ignore explicit user choices.

### Acceptance criteria

- The role lists every required assessment dimension and records a concise rationale for its chosen workflow.
- Direct, decomposed, and adversarial paths are distinct and proportional, without a fixed global threshold or agent count.
- Decomposition contracts include dependencies, ownership, deliverables, allowed scope, protected state, checks, and stopping conditions.
- Feasible user-specified orchestration is followed exactly; a conflicting constraint is disclosed without silent substitution.

### Planned verification

- Run focused contract checks for all assessment dimensions and all three workflow paths.
- Exercise static scenarios for simple, decomposable-complex, uncertain-nondecomposable, feasible user override, and constrained user override cases.
- Review the file diff for changes outside the generic reusable role.

## TASK-005 - Define durable orchestration and stopping records

Specify how the reusable Task and Director contracts record classification, decomposition or adversarial decisions, role and child identities, reviews, revisions, synthesis, implementation ownership, blockers, and completion evidence while keeping all state systems distinct.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Status | `completed` |
| State reason | None |
| Skip authority | None |
| Requirements | REQ-003, REQ-017, REQ-018, REQ-019, REQ-020, REQ-022 |
| Design basis | None |
| Target artifacts | SKILLS-depo/task/SKILL.md, ROLES-depo/project-director-ROLE.md |
| Dependencies | TASK-004 |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | 2026-09-02T21:33:57.686548Z |

### Risks

- A prose-only record requirement could conflict with the canonical Agent Task schema.
- The workflow could retain private deliberative content or treat child state as Task state.

### Acceptance criteria

- The contracts identify the governed Task record and Task Responses as the durable continuation record without inventing an unauthorized second ledger.
- Every required orchestration event has a concise record location or an explicit impact dependency on Agent Task.
- Task, subtask, child, TRD, plan, conversation, native goal, Git, deployment, and release states remain separate.
- Iteration continues only for a materially new hypothesis, evidence item, or targeted revision; otherwise the exact blocker or user decision is recorded.

### Planned verification

- Trace each required orchestration event to a governed record field or response section.
- Check the contracts retain only concise decisions and evidence and reject full transcripts, stale memory, and child status as canonical evidence.
- Run no-progress, missing-authority, missing-capability, and runtime-limit scenarios.
